compatibleChanges.rationale: Retains the additive optional commandId plus device-pairing and command-receipt request variants while sharing the existing attachment declarations with canonical timeline payloads. Existing request fields and variants remain unchanged; older daemons continue parsing old requests and reject only newly invoked RPC variants they do not implement. The compaction timeline item additionally gains optional outcome and error fields; its status enum stays loading|completed, so an older app parses every terminal compaction exactly as before and simply ignores the refinement. Daseo adds the agent.side_question.request variant (/btw side questions); a new request type that older daemons reject as unknown, and newer clients send it only when server_info.features.sideQuestion is true. Daseo browser automation (deltas 26 and 28) changes the browser.automation.execute.response and hello capability shapes the app sends to the daemon. Tab info gains an optional loadingForMs; an older daemon's non-strict object schema strips it and parses the list_tabs reply as before. The result union gains a network variant (browser_network capture: action, capturing, optional entries with seq/method/url/resourceType/status/mimeType/failed/startedAt/durationMs/requestHeaders/bodies, optional cursor/hasMore/pendingCount/droppedCount). An older daemon would reject that unknown result command, so compatibility rests on never sending it: the app returns a network result only in reply to a network request, which an older daemon has no tool to issue. A newer app advertises network in browserHost.supportedCommands, and an older daemon's capability parser drops unknown command names (checked: ["snapshot","future_cmd"] parses to ["snapshot"]). Daseo browser tools (delta 34) change the browser.automation.execute.response shapes the app sends to the daemon. The wait result's matched enum widens to text|url|selector|script|load; navigate, back, forward, and reload results gain optional httpStatus and httpStatusText, and back/forward/reload an optional url (an older daemon's non-strict object schema strips them and reports the navigation as before; navigate.url stays a required string and now holds the committed URL after redirects). The result union gains read (url, title, format markdown, scope main|page|ref, content, truncated, stats chars/links/structuredDataFound) and find (matches of optional ref, role, name, states, optional landmark/text; total) variants. An older daemon never receives them: the app returns read/find results only in reply to read/find requests, which an older daemon has no tool to issue, and a widened matched value only answers a wait with a selector, script, or load condition, which an older daemon cannot send. A newer app advertises read and find in browserHost.supportedCommands; an older daemon's capability parser drops unknown command names. Daseo 0.5.46 (delta 34 follow-up) adds an optional read-result mainFallback (product_page | no_article), which an older daemon's non-strict object schema strips, and widens the wait result's matched enum with networkidle. A 0.5.45 daemon would reject a networkidle match from a newer app and time that one wait out; the desktop host ships in the same bundle as its daemon, so that pairing does not occur, and 0.5.44 and older daemons cannot request networkidle at all. Daseo 0.5.47 (delta 35) adds optional fields to results the app sends: a console log entry's previousPage and a resize result's emulation (mobile, userAgent, deviceScaleFactor); an older daemon's non-strict object schemas strip both. The result union gains a styles variant (ref, element, rules of selector/optional source/line/conditions/inheritedFrom and declarations name/value/optional important/overridden/invalid, computed, userAgentRules, truncated); the app returns it only in reply to a styles request, which an older daemon has no tool to issue.

Retains the additive optional turnOutcome, feature flags, device-pairing, push-catch-up, and command-receipt responses, and adds optional imageCount and attachments to canonical user timeline rows. Existing response fields and variants remain unchanged; older clients ignore optional object fields and never receive new RPC responses unless they send the corresponding new request. The compaction timeline item additionally gains optional outcome and error fields; its status enum stays loading|completed, so an older app parses every terminal compaction exactly as before and simply ignores the refinement. The compaction timeline item also gains an optional turnId (Daseo 6ef0fdbb1) that older apps ignore. Canonical user timeline rows additionally gain one optional origin field ("system") marking Paseo system prompts; all existing fields and variants remain unchanged, and an older app ignores the optional field and renders the row as a plain user message. Daseo adds the agent.side_question.response variant, sent only in reply to agent.side_question.request, and the optional server_info.features.sideQuestion flag that older apps ignore. Daseo browser automation (delta 28) adds a network variant to the browser.automation.execute.request command union (action start|stop|list; optional urlIncludes, method, resourceType, since; primitive defaults for maxEntries, includeBodies, includeRequestBodies). An older app's generated outbound validator rejects an unknown command: the client logs "Message validation failed" and drops that one message (checked against the generated validator), so the variant is not tolerated as unknown data. Compatibility rests on the capability gate instead: the broker sends a command only to a host whose browserHost.supportedCommands includes it (unsupportedCommandFailure runs before sendRequest), older apps derive that list from their own command names and never advertise network, so they get no request and the agent receives browser_unsupported. Existing command and result variants are unchanged; the iframe snapshot work (delta 27) changes no wire schema. Daseo background waits (delta 30) add one optional backgroundWaits object ({ pending: nonnegative integer, labels: string[] }) to agent snapshot and agent list item payloads; all existing fields and variants remain unchanged, and an older app's non-strict object schema strips the field and shows an idle agent exactly as before. Daseo browser tools (delta 34) add read and find variants to the browser.automation.execute.request command union (read: scope main|page default main, optional ref, links default true, maxChars default 40000 max 120000; find: optional role/name with a role-or-name refine, exact default false, limit default 10 max 50), gated like network: the broker sends them only to a host whose browserHost.supportedCommands lists them, and older apps never advertise them, so the agent gets browser_unsupported. The wait command args gain optional selector, script, and load (load|networkidle), and the exactly-one-condition refine now counts all five. An older app's validator rejects a wait that uses a new condition (strict args, old refine), so that one request would be dropped and time out; this is accepted because the browser host is only the desktop app, which ships in the same Daseo bundle as the daemon it starts (Android and web never register as browser hosts), and an existing text or url wait is unchanged on the wire. Daseo 0.5.47 (delta 35) adds optional command args: snapshot ref and interactive, screenshot ref, logs level (debug|info|warning|error), and resize mobile, userAgent, and deviceScaleFactor; it adds a styles command (browserId, ref, optional properties, maxRules default 30 max 100) gated like read and find through browserHost.supportedCommands. An older app's strict args reject a request that uses a new field, so that one request fails; the browser host is only the desktop app shipped in the same bundle as the daemon, and requests without the new fields are unchanged on the wire.
Adds one optional E2EE v2 metadata object while retaining v:2, serverId, daemonPublicKeyB64, and relay unchanged, so older clients parse the same offer and use the legacy authenticated channel.
